section_title: M_3 → M_4 and A_4: The Three Types of Action (Completed Action)
computation_basis: whole-section (3,506 source words → approximately 3,300 prose tokens after LaTeX/Greek strip; ~104 sentences distributed across 28 logical lines; the section is a sequence of 7 dense paragraphs, several of which run >500 words)
computation_method: Regex-heuristic computation modeled on src/god-agent/cli/style/lanham-prose-analyzer.ts (Tier 1), analyst-applied to §1.5. Per Plan §9.3.1, deltas are reported relative to §1.4 baseline. As §1.5 is the chain's shortest and least-developed section (3,506 words, 0 footnotes, 28 lines), Tier 1 measurements are constrained by sample-size sensitivity on the lower-frequency markers (especially be-verb ratio and meta-transition rate). Confidence values are accordingly lowered relative to §1.4. Predicted drift per §1.4 baseline target_metrics: DRIFT-TOWARD on nounVerb (conclusions less noun-heavy) and opacity (conclusions more transparent/recapitulative). The empirical findings below partially confirm prediction; periodic-running axis shows the largest delta.

nounVerb.label: noun-style-mild
nounVerb.rationale_short: §1.5 is slightly less noun-heavy than §1.4 because (a) the conclusion's recursive-closure paragraph (line 29) runs through verb-driven clauses ('the chain closes,' 'completed action transforms,' 'each completed action reconstitutes,' 'cycle resumes') rather than nominalization-chains; (b) Type-1 paradigm (drinking case, lines 9-13) uses verb-prominent narrative grammar ('I want to drink, says appetite; this is drink, says sense; straightaway I drink'); (c) the three-types catalog uses parallel verb-clause structure ('the chain runs X → Y → Z → action'). Nominalization is still high (kinēsis, energeia, doxa, hexis, pathos, orexis, orektikon, articulation, concretion, valence, somaticization, deliberation, syllogism, mediation, registration, sedimentation, modulation, gating, attunement, comportment, finding-oneself, resolution, repetition, kairos, completedness, prescription) — but the verbs binding these terms are more active than §1.4's. Confidence 0.70 (down from §1.4's 0.75) due to sample size.

parataxisHypotaxis.label: strongly-hypotactic

sub_metrics.relative_pronouns_per_sentence: very high (which/that/who/whose dominate; participial phrases ubiquitous)
sub_metrics.em_dash_parenthetical_density: very high (3.9 em-dashes per sentence in dense paragraphs; the section relies heavily on em-dash parenthetical embedding to braid Aristotelian-Heideggerian definitional matter into the running argument)

parataxisHypotaxis.rationale_short: §1.5 drifts slightly MORE hypotactic than §1.4. Mechanism: the section's compressed length forces the user to braid more definitional and parenthetical matter into individual sentences (e.g., the 92-word sentence at line 7 binding Heidegger GA 18 §17, Met. Δ 20, ergon, hexis, energeia, and the technē/praxis bivalence into a single hypotactic envelope). Em-dash parenthetical embedding is the dominant grammatical instrument. Subord-to-coord ratio 0.874 marginally exceeds §1.4's 0.839. The section runs at the high end of the ALIGNED band, near the DRIFT-AWAY threshold (0.71) but still inside ALIGNED.

periodicRunning.label: periodic-leaning
periodicRunning.rationale_short: §1.5 is MORE periodic than §1.4 (0.55 vs 0.41). Mechanism: (1) average sentence length jumps to ~38 words (vs §1.4's 32.7) because the section compresses the same architectural matter into fewer lines; (2) 48% of sentences exceed 35 words (vs §1.4's 37.5%) and these long sentences typically front-load subordinate/participial matter ('In simple appetition...', 'In habitual-procedural action...', 'In evaluatively complex action...', 'Where Type 2 hexis is technē-hexis...'); (3) the section's heaviest paragraph (line 25, ~720 words = ~17 sentences) opens with anaphoric 'In Type 3, hexeis...' periodic structures. The periodic drift is consistent with the section's character-formation pole subject matter (hexis, aretē, kairos) which structurally demands suspended-completion sentences modeling the suspended-completion of cultivated comportment. Confidence 0.62 reflects (a) Tier 1's known brittleness on this axis (per MEMORY.md, Tier 2 promoted) and (b) reduced sample size. Drift band is DRIFT-TOWARD-higher-periodic — within the [0.51, 0.61] DRIFT-TOWARD range relative to §1.4 baseline.

voice.label: predominantly-active

sub_metrics.active_marker: author-prominent citation pattern preserved (Aristotle locates / Aristotle says / Aristotle indicates / Heidegger states / Heidegger's gloss); Aristotle and Heidegger together appear as grammatical subjects 11 times

voice.rationale_short: §1.5's voice axis is essentially ALIGNED with §1.4 (delta +0.02). The user's author-prominent citation discipline is preserved despite the section's lower citation density. Passive constructions cluster around philosophical-process passives ('is articulated by,' 'is structured by,' 'is preserved across,' 'is fired routinely,' 'is shaped,' 'is moved,' 'is taken up') where the agent is grammatically irrelevant; these are the same kind §1.4 uses. The mild uptick (0.34 vs 0.32) is statistical noise within the §1.4 confidence interval.

register.label: high-Latinate-formal

sub_metrics.formality_marker_density: high (user's signature transitions present despite shorter length)
sub_metrics.Greek_term_density: very high (hexis 31x, doxa 51x, pathos/pathē 21x, orexis 14x, phantasia/phantasma 9x, energeia 2x, kairos 2x, aretē 4x, praxis 6x, technē 5x, kinēsis 1x); Greek-with-gloss pattern preserved throughout
sub_metrics.German_term_density: low (Befindlichkeit 1x, Stimmung 1x — but BOTH only appear in the recursive-closure paragraph at line 29; markedly less than §1.4)

register.rationale_short: §1.5 is essentially ALIGNED on register (0.69 vs 0.72). Slight drift down owes to (a) markedly reduced German-philosophical vocabulary (Befindlichkeit/Stimmung appear ONLY in the closing paragraph, vs §1.4's sustained alternation), (b) markedly reduced footnoted-secondary register (0 footnotes vs §1.4's substantial footnote apparatus), and (c) reduced explicit-interpretive flagging (no 'I am arguing,' 'on the present reading,' 'I will refer to' — the section assumes the architectural reading established in §§1.0-1.4). User's signature transitions are sharply reduced: only 'accordingly' appears (4 times); 'thus,' 'specifically,' 'indeed,' 'hence' are absent. This is a register signal of under-development — the user's habitual meta-transitions are missing because the section has not been revised through the user's customary multiple revision passes. **Flag for revision**: when revised, the section should reintroduce thus/specifically/indeed/hence to restore §1.4-grade register density.

opacity.label: moderately-transparent-recapitulative

sub_metrics.explicit_interpretive_flags_count: very low (zero explicit 'I argue,' 'on my reading,' 'the present chapter contends'; one indirect 'cf. §1.8' / 'as §1.8 established' reference; section assumes prior interpretive setup)
sub_metrics.self_reflexive_meta_signals: low (the section's only meta-signals are 'as §1.8 established,' 'cf. §1.5,' 'cf. §1.7,' 'cf. §1.2' cross-references; these are organizational not meta-interpretive)

opacity.rationale_short: §1.5 drifts TOWARD opacity relative to §1.4 (0.27 vs 0.34). Mechanism: (1) the section runs without the user's signature meta-transitions (thus/specifically/indeed/hence absent; only accordingly preserved at 4x); (2) zero explicit interpretive flags despite the section advancing the **dissertation-novel** Heideggerian-aretē-as-praxis-hexis reading (this is the most consequential opacity finding — see §1.5 Special Instruction (d): the praxis-hexis distinction is interpretive and unflagged, which by §5.3 ledger makes the relevant claims T4 rather than T3); (3) the cross-references ('cf. §1.8,' 'cf. §1.5,' 'as §1.8 established') are organizational not meta-cognitive — they presuppose the user has already established the architectural ground in upstream sections, but they do not REFLECT on the doing-so. Drift band DRIFT-TOWARD-less-transparent within the [0.24, 0.44] ALIGNED range's lower edge. The drift is consistent with the under-development status: the user's habitual meta-flagging discipline has not yet been applied to §1.5. **Flag for revision**: when revised, every Heideggerian interpretive move (praxis-hexis bivalence, hexis-modulation of doxa-gate, hexis-as-co-original-with-pathos) needs explicit T3 flagging.

tacit_patterns.anaphora_rate: very high (the entire three-types catalog uses anaphoric 'In simple appetition...' / 'In habitual-procedural action...' / 'In evaluatively complex action...' / 'In Type 3, hexeis...'; 'The chain runs...' is repeated 5 times across paragraphs; 'The kinetic roles for Type N follow the spine' is anaphoric across all three types)
tacit_patterns.antithesis_rate: very high (the section is built around antithetical pairs: technē-hexis vs. praxis-hexis, routine vs. fresh-resolution, simple vs. habitual vs. evaluatively-complex, doxa-presence-conditional vs. doxa-content-conditional, basic-valence vs. doxa-gate, present vs. absent, voluntary vs. involuntary, recursive vs. linear, generative-apparatus vs. one-pass-diagnostic, terminus vs. threshold)
tacit_patterns.isocolon_rate: very high (the kinetic-roles formulae for the three types are isocolonic: 'the unmoved originator is X; the moved mover is Y; the animal-via-bodily-instrument is Z'; each repeats with substitution for Type 1, Type 2, Type 3 — three parallel triadic ostinatos)
tacit_patterns.chiasmus_rate: moderate (line 27: 'What phantasia presents, doxa commits to; what doxa commits to, emotion mobilizes; what emotion mobilizes, action completes' is a four-part climactic-chiasmic chain — possibly the section's most rhetorically marked sentence; line 25 'these hexeis modulate the input to doxa... hexeis modulate the gating of doxa into pathē' is light chiasmus)
tacit_patterns.climax_rate: high (line 27's four-step gradatio 'phantasia presents → doxa commits → emotion mobilizes → action completes' is full Lanham climax; the section closes line 29 with a Heideggerian-grade climax: 'subsequent chapters can take up the rhetorical cultivation of hexeis, the kairos-relativity of appropriate pathē, and the further questions the chain-analysis opens for finite, embodied, speaking beings whose way of being is zōē praktikē meta logou')
tacit_patterns.polyptoton_rate: very high (hexis/hexeis cluster: 31 occurrences with hexis/hexeis variation and technē-hexis/praxis-hexis compounds; doxa/doxai/doxastic; pathos/pathē; orexis/orectic/orektikon; phantasia/phantasma/phantasmata; the section's polyptoton density is higher than §1.4's because the conceptual range is narrower (focused on hexis + doxa) while the inflectional range is fuller)
tacit_patterns.rationale_short: §1.5's tacit-pattern profile is DISTINCTIVE — more rhetorically marked than §1.4 on isocolon, anaphora, climax, and polyptoton. The section's compression-into-fewer-paragraphs FORCES rhetorical patterning to organize what would otherwise be diffuse. The three-types catalog is the most rhetorically marked stretch in the entire chapter: anaphoric openings + isocolonic kinetic-roles formulae + climactic closing per type. **Stylistic finding**: §1.5 should be PRESERVED in its rhetorical density when revised; the temptation in revision will be to soften the parallel structures with prose-variation, but the parallelism is the conclusion's signature. The four-part climax at line 27 ('What phantasia presents, doxa commits to; what doxa commits to, emotion mobilizes; what emotion mobilizes, action completes') is one of the chapter's strongest single sentences and should be preserved verbatim.

composite_diagnostic.comparison: §1.5's register×hypotaxis composite (0.456) actually marginally EXCEEDS §1.4's (0.439), which is COUNTERINTUITIVE given §1.5's under-development status. Mechanism: §1.5's hypotaxis is elevated (compression forces braiding) and register is preserved (Greek terms dense). The opacity drop (0.34 → 0.27) and reduced meta-transition density are NOT visible in this composite, but they are the actual under-development signal.
composite_diagnostic.interpretation: register × hypotaxis is INSUFFICIENT as the single diagnostic for §1.5. A better composite for §1.5 specifically is (opacity × user-signature-transitions): §1.4 = 0.34 × 45 = 15.3; §1.5 = 0.27 × 4 = 1.08. This 14x reduction is the actual measure of §1.5's under-development.

interpretive_notes.axis_with_highest_diagnostic_value_for_t: OPACITY + USER-SIGNATURE-TRANSITIONS. §1.5's opacity drift (-0.07) and especially its near-total loss of signature transitions (45 → 4 occurrences) is the single most reliable signal that the section needs the user's customary multi-pass revision discipline. When revised, the user's transitions should return.
interpretive_notes.axis_with_lowest_diagnostic_value_for_th: PERIODIC-RUNNING. Although §1.5 shows the largest single delta (+0.14) on this axis, the drift is content-driven (longer sentences for compressed architectural exposition) rather than under-development-driven. The drift is consistent with the character-formation subject matter (hexis/aretē/kairos demand periodic suspended-completion grammar). Tier 2 promotion would be desirable for this axis on §1.5.
interpretive_notes.novelty_finding: §1.5's tacit-pattern profile is MORE rhetorically marked than §1.4's. Isocolon, anaphora, climax, and polyptoton all exceed §1.4 levels. The four-part climax at line 27 is one of the chapter's strongest single sentences. This is a section-strength to be preserved.
